final_assessment: "Drop this" is now a first-class exploration outcome, captured into rc13a (the declaration) and rc13b (the readout) rather than a third stage. Verified before capturing: no explore path defines a no-change outcome — the only exit is promotion to a change, and Considered & out rejects options WITHIN an exploration, never the exploration itself — and every rung of the maturity grid points at continuing or building, so an exploration that has decided not to build must fight its own readout to say so. That is the same defect as the top rung asserting readiness on heading count, sitting in the surface whose job is to help decide whether to build at all. The program layer already had the concept (rc11 moved to Considered & out with a re-entry trigger, recorded as a good outcome) and the exploration layer had no equivalent verb. Evidence from the day: two stages ran full propose-review-archive cycles and shipped nothing, and rc13a's own second attempt might have concluded at explore — R-crc-10 would have told it to — but there was no way to say so and have the workflow agree. Dropping at explore costs one sitting; dropping at archive cost three passes, twice. Captured into two existing stages because the declaration is convention and the readout is the emit's, and a third stage editing the same two capabilities is how a requirement gets three owners.
